title: Positioning Persona Memory: Bounded Cross-Session Context vs. Retrieval-Based Long-Term Memory
description:
A targeted literature discovery pass to support the positioning argument for
Persona Memory (PM), a bounded (<=270 token) cross-session context system for
enterprise AI agents. PM injects a single structured summary once at session
start rather than retrieving facts from a large accumulated history. This
review is seeded from two clusters: (1) "Beyond pass@1" (Goh et al. reading,
2603.29231), which finds that unbounded intra-task memory scaffolds injected
every turn universally hurt long-horizon agent performance and explicitly
calls for alternative bounded/structured memory architectures as future work;
and (2) the current cross-session user-memory benchmark literature
(PersonaMem, MemoryCD, LoCoMo, LongMemEval), which uniformly frames the
problem as retrieval accuracy from large (100K+ token) histories rather than
as bounded structured context injection. The goal is to find any literature
that (a) already proposes bounded/non-retrieval alternatives to long-history
retrieval for cross-session memory, (b) evaluates memory quality by
downstream task/response quality rather than retrieval accuracy, or (c)
frames persistent agent memory as a governance/auditability problem for
enterprise deployment rather than a personalization problem -- so we can
correctly claim novelty (or concede prior art) for PM's positioning.
criteria:
Include papers primarily addressing the novel architecture, mechanisms, or active management strategies of external, persistent memory systems specifically designed for LLM agents, enabling knowledge accumulation and retention across distinct interactions or sessions. The core contribution must be to the design, implementation, or evaluation of such a memory system, rather than its application as a secondary component within broader personalization, dialogue generation, or general agent capabilities. This excludes memory systems focused solely on the LLM's internal mechanisms or short-term, intra-session context management.

Specifically, this includes:
1. Personalization, active management (selection, consolidation, summarization), or bounded/unbounded representations within such memory architectures, including session summarization or hierarchical/recursive summaries.
2. Benchmarks, evaluations, or reliability frameworks specifically assessing the performance, capabilities, or failure modes of these LLM agent memory systems, particularly regarding long-term knowledge accumulation.
3. Governance aspects like auditability, accountability, or observability of persistent agent state/context.

Exclude:
1. Papers primarily focused on general agent capabilities (e.g., reasoning, planning, tool use, dialogue) or LLM internal mechanisms (e.g., KV cache, attention, long context window performance), where the memory system is not the central architectural or mechanistic contribution for long-term knowledge accumulation.
2. Papers primarily focused on optimizing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or other pure retrieval mechanisms, knowledge-graph construction, multimodal input processing, persona simulation, or personalization methods (e.g., fine-tuning, DPO, prompt engineering), if their primary contribution is to the specific mechanism itself, rather than to the architecture or active management of an LLM agent's persistent memory system for cross-session knowledge accumulation and retention.
3. Multi-agent systems, hardware optimization, or surveys/reviews not proposing novel memory system architectures or evaluation frameworks.
